name: International Jewish conspiracy
scope: The modern, political belief that a hidden, worldwide Jewish group ("International Jewry") secretly directs states, finance, the press and revolutions toward world domination, as the scholarship defines it (Bangerter et al. in the Routledge Handbook, ch. on antisemitism and conspiracism; Rathje 2021; John 1996): a belief whose content is highly variable, traced from the 1797-1806 Barruel/Simonini Illuminati claims through Goedsche's novel Biarritz (1868) to The Protocols of the Elders of Zion (c. 1903), Henry Ford's The International Jew, Nazi propaganda and post-1945 variants (fiscal, Holocaust-denial, anti-Zionist). The scope is the tenets of this world-conspiracy belief as its own proponents state them (Carr, Simpson and the Pakistani Faruqi, each in the texts cited, which name 'International Jewry' or 'the Jewish conspiracy') and as the scholarship records them. It excludes the medieval religious accusations (blood libel, host desecration) except as the scholarship's background, the separate tropes the sources treat as adjacent (Judeo-Bolshevism, Judeo-Masonry, Cultural Marxism, ZOG) as sources in their own right, and critics, who do not answer.

summary: The international Jewish conspiracy is the belief that a hidden, worldwide Jewish group secretly directs governments, finance, the press and revolutions in pursuit of world domination. Its content is highly variable (religious, financial, communist, Masonic, anti-Zionist and Holocaust-denying versions), which the scholarship says is what lets it spread and last; the Protocols of the Elders of Zion made it the core myth of modern antisemitism and of Nazi propaganda. As a belief about a plot, it states a single political claim, that a minority is secretly conspiring against nations; the sources say nothing settled on the test's other questions.
